page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.4xlarge is an ARM64-based compute-optimized server powered by an AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and includes 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. Network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth managed via the Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong memory subsystem performance, achieving a top-tier Passmark memory score and strong uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths of 296.81 GB/sec and 124.13 GB/sec, respectively. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is highly efficient at 203.34 GB/sec. However, while database operations and small-model LLM inference perform at average to strong levels, prompt processing for medium 7B LLM models is a relative bottleneck, registering a weaker score of 31.26 tokens/sec.

The c8gd.4xlarge offers high resource density for compute-intensive workloads that benefit from local NVMe storage. By utilizing custom ARM64 architecture, it provides a cost-efficient alternative to traditional x86 architectures for workloads requiring high memory bandwidth and fast local disk access. This server is well-suited for database operations, multi-threaded data compression, static web serving, and general compute tasks, though it is less optimal for heavy large-language model inference.
